subject: Spectra Labs — end-to-end latency targets & POC kickoff checklist
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samuel Perez <samuel.perez@spectralabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Spectra Labs — end-to-end latency targets & POC kickoff checklist

Hi Samuel — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned before we kick off the POC.

Summary from call:
- Current incumbent (VendorX) observed p95 ~ 420 ms, p99 ~ 1.1 s (measured end-to-end from Spectra app in us-west).
- Typical request profile: 150–350 tokens, median payload ~ 2.3 KB; occasional 1k token bursts for longer-generation jobs.
- Target traffic: steady-state 60 req/s, peak spikes to 180 req/s for short windows (1–3 min).
- Streaming: partial-token streaming enabled in ~40% of requests (low-latency UI streaming is critical).

What we need to validate in the POC (proposed acceptance criteria):
1) End-to-end (app -> Redwood hosted API -> client) p95 <= 300 ms; p99 <= 650 ms under baseline traffic (60 req/s) for streaming-enabled workload.
2) Maintain p95 <= 450 ms, p99 <= 900 ms during 3x burst (180 req/s) with <= 2s tail degradation.
3) Concurrent KV-cache warm sessions & streaming concurrency of at least 12 without >20% throughput loss.
4) Throughput: sustain 60 req/s with median response size ~200 tokens for 30+ minutes.

Attachments: I’ve attached a lightweight test plan and a short streaming behavior summary for Redwood hosted (spectra_latency_test_plan.pdf; redwood_streaming_summary.xlsx).

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm the acceptance criteria above or send counter-targets by Thu 11/5.
- Procurement sends any standard NDA/PO/contract items to procurement@spectralabs.com (cc’d).
- We schedule a POC kickoff (30–60 min) next week to align test windows and access.

If that looks good I’ll book a slot and loop in our SRE/POC engineer.

Thanks,
Olga

From: Samuel Perez <samuel.perez@spectralabs.com>

Date: Tue, 03 Nov 2026 17:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spectra Labs — end-to-end latency targets & POC kickoff checklist

Thanks, Olga — good summary. A few clarifications and details from our side: 

- The incumbent numbers I quoted were collected from our staging environment (us-west) during peak traffic last month — p95 ~420 ms, p99 ~1.1 s. We can share the raw traces after the NDA.
- Payload mix: 70% short (<=200 tokens), 25% medium (200–600), 5% long (>600). Burst windows typically coincide with our batch ingestion (every 10 min) and a marketing-driven flash event.
- Streaming behavior: our client renders token deltas as they arrive; we need first-token time (TT1) < 120 ms for good UX, and steady streaming increments thereafter.
- Security/procurement: procurement@spectralabs.com will handle contractual items. We prefer a 30-day POC with a runbook and a simple ticket for support during tests.

I’ll review the acceptance criteria you proposed and send comments by Thursday. Meanwhile procurement, can you start an NDA?

—Samuel
Samuel Perez
Head of Platform, Spectra Labs
samuel.perez@spectralabs.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 04 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: internal: quick alignment on Spectra POC config

Olga / Marissa — quick internal note before we respond to Samuel’s details. My suggested POC configuration and talking points: 

- Baseline POC model: quantized Llama-3-medium variant (matches their token profile). Expect better streaming TT1 vs incumbent because of optimized streaming kernels and prefix caching.
- Network topology: serve from us-west region to match their staging. Use 4x concurrent stream workers per pod, target streaming concurrency 12 across 3 pods (scale policy allows burst to 5 pods).
- QoS targets we can commit to for POC marketing materials: p95 <= 280 ms, p99 <= 600 ms under baseline 60 req/s non-adversarial load. Emphasize that network e2e time depends on client path; recommend we measure from Spectra’s app agents.
- Test infra: provide a lightweight test harness (curl + scripted token stream) and a perf dashboard link for live metrics.

If that sounds right I’ll draft the POC runbook and timing.

-ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samuel Perez <samuel.perez@spectralabs.com>, procurement@spectralabs.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Nov 2026 08:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Spectra Labs — end-to-end latency targets & POC kickoff checklist

Samuel / Procurement — thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple edits to the acceptance criteria based on Ben’s note (below):

Updated acceptance criteria for POC (what we’ll validate):
- Measurement window: 30m sustained baseline (60 req/s) + 10m burst (180 req/s).
- Streaming UX: first-token latency (TT1) measured from Spectra client <= 120 ms for >= 90% of requests during baseline.
- End-to-end: p95 <= 300 ms, p99 <= 650 ms during baseline; p95 <= 500 ms, p99 <= 950 ms during burst.
- Concurrency: support 12 simultaneous streaming sessions without >20% throughput degradation.

Logistics:
- POC length: 30 days with a 7-day ramp to steady-state.
- Data/Access: we’ll need a staging API key and a test user-agent to run the harness.
- Measurement: we’ll provide a live dashboard and weekly perf snapshots; we ask Spectra to run one distributed trace dump at the start and one at the end of each major test window.

Proposed schedule:
- Thu 11/5: procurement to send NDA (procurement@spectralabs.com)
- Mon 11/9: 30–45 min kickoff to align runbook and test windows
- Tue 11/10 – Wed 12/09: POC run (with agreed check-ins)

Please confirm the schedule and the acceptance criteria so Ben and I can finalize the runbook and provisioning.

Best,
Olga
Olga Petrov
